Unlike traditional AI-assisted development methods, AI-DLC reimagines the entire software lifecycle through two key dimensions: AI-powered execution with human oversight and dynamic team collaboration. Al6P92NNHf8.label: re:Invent 2025 breakouts
Al6P92NNHf8.description:
The NFL and AWS have developed new Next Gen Stats that leverage advanced Machine Learning models to analyze defensive coverages in NFL football games. Using spatio-temporal transformer architectures with factorized attention mechanisms, the system produces three key metrics: individual coverage assignments, receiver-defender matchups, and target defender identification on pass plays. This multi-faceted approach enables comprehensive analysis of defensive strategies, from pre-snap alignments to evolving coverage responsibilities as plays unfold. By automating the complex task of coverage analysis through advanced AI modeling, these new statistics provide unprecedented insights into defensive tactics, player performance evaluation, and offensive decision-making. K0dqsUVlkks.description:
The NBA is launching a new advanced stats program, “Inside The Game, Powered by AWS”  to bring fans closer to the game of basketball. During every NBA game, billions of data points are captured, such as a player’s scoring performance on every shot, to their skeletal pose location on the court 60 times a second. This data is used in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) models to create advanced stats and insights that go beyond the usual box score. This session will cover the NBA’s advanced stats platform migration from Azure to AWS and how the suite of AI/ML based stats are being developed. It will also cover how the NBA partnered with AWS to build the new “Gravity” Inside The Game stat, which leverages existing NBA advanced stats and a predictive ML model to determine how much a player pulls defense towards them in real-time throughout every offensive possession.

Caching has evolved beyond key-value lookups. Modern applications demand flexibility and extreme performance. Redis 8 introduces two major innovations: Client-side caching, which solves the “hot keys” problem by storing frequently accessed data near the application and cascading invalidations for scalability under load; and the Redis Query Engine, enabling search across nested JSON and complex data types. Redis 8.4 further reduces JSON memory usage and adds new commands. Combined with Redis Data Integration (RDI), Redis now serves as a high-speed data layer for real-time apps in e-commerce, healthcare, fintech, and AI. iFood is joining this session to share their Redis journey. nPyuVZ9rkWk.title: AWS re:Invent 2025 - Cyber resilience on AWS, designing security and recovery strategies (GBL204)
nPyuVZ9rkWk.label: re:Invent 2025 breakouts
nPyuVZ9rkWk.description:
Cyber resilience is the ability of an organization to continuously deliver the intended outcome despite adverse cyber events. It has an overlap with disaster recovery where both cyber resilience and disaster recovery involve plans and actions to restore normal operations after an incident. Cyber resilience includes disaster recovery as part of its broader strategy.
There are multiple key themes when it comes to designing for cyber resilience:
- Protect: Proactive measures taken to safeguard systems, networks, and data.
- Prepare: Activities to ensure an organization can effectively respond to and recover from a cyber incident.
- Recover: Actions taken to restore systems, networks, and data to their normal state after a cyber incident.

zbN1VeenxY4.title: AWS re:Invent 2025 - Transforming Apache Kafka into a Scalable Message Queue (OPN413)
zbN1VeenxY4.label: re:Invent 2025 breakouts
zbN1VeenxY4.description:
Event streaming in Apache Kafka is powerful, but sometimes a queue-based model is more suited for workloads where parallel consumption is more important than ordering. KIP-932 introduces share groups, a feature that allows consumers to cooperatively consume data from Kafka topics, akin to how message queues work. This enables per-message acknowledgment, retries, and load distribution without the complexities of partition management. Ideal for independent work items, this approach simplifies message handling and enhances scalability. Join us to learn how KIP-932 brings queuing semantics to Kafka, enabling more flexible, efficient processing in event-driven architectures.
